$comment: D-EXAMPLES-RUNNER-MULTI-ARTIFACT (c171): the FIRST multi-artifact corpus example, across FOUR targets. Each target's `dependsOn` builds `dsslib.c` (exporting dss_lib_answer) into a STATIC LIBRARY via the c171-D `-staticlib` format (a `.lib` on pe64 / a `.a` on elf64 x86_64 + aarch64 and on macho64 arm64), then builds `main.c` (extern dss_lib_answer) RESOLVING against it via --resolve-library -> the c169/c170 COFF / c165 ELF static-link pulls the member into a SELF-CONTAINED exec -> exit 42. Witnesses, at the corpus tier + end-to-end: the c171 dependsOn runner capability, the c171-D staticlib driver surface, and the static-link pull/merge. RUNTIME per leg: PE runs natively on the Windows gate; ELF x86_64 runs natively under WSL / on the ubuntu leg; ELF aarch64 runs under qemu-aarch64 (the emulator) / on the ubuntu-24.04-arm leg -- the arm64 arm is the runnable witness that CLOSES D-LK-STATIC-LINK-AARCH64-RUNTIME (arm64 static-link had been build-only); MACH-O arm64 runs NATIVELY on the darwin leg. SkippedCrossHost where a leg cannot run, with the BUILD still giving structural coverage. D-TEST-EXAMPLES-DEPENDSON-UNCOVERED-ON-DARWIN: the macho64 arm is the entry that makes the `dependsOn` path RUN on darwin at all. Before it, NEITHER dependsOn manifest carried a `darwin` runOn, so integrated_tests' `buildDependsOnArtifactCli` -- which SKIPS an example outright when no target's runOn matches the host -- was reached by ZERO checks on the leg this project gates on every cycle: a whole build path free to rot while the suite reported green. MEASURED on darwin arm64: dsslib.a (422 B) built, main linked resolving it, spawned -> exit 42. RED-ON-DISABLE (MEASURED, same host): drop the `--resolve-library` (i.e. lose the dependsOn thread) and main STILL links -- DSS does not yet fail loud on an undefined exec symbol (the open D-LINK-EXEC-UNDEFINED-SYMBOL-FAIL-LOUD gap) -- but dyld aborts at RUNTIME with `Symbol not found: _dss_lib_answer` -> exit 134 != 42 -> the exit-code assert fires -> red. So 42 here is a real function of the archive pull, not a constant. D-EXAMPLES-DEPENDSON-NO-RELEASE-OPTIMIZER-ARM (the `release` arm below): this manifest and fat_archive_merge's are the corpus's ONLY two that use the runner's per-target `dependsOn` key, and until now NEITHER declared an `optimizedPipelines` arm -- so the whole `dependsOn` / `-staticlib` / `--resolve-library` static-link path had only ever been compiled through the baseline pipeline, which is a bare `Identity`, i.e. a no-op. WHAT THE ARM IS FOR: with the runner building each prerequisite library under the arm's OWN configuration, the `release` arm compiles `dsslib.c` through the shipped release pipeline as well as `main.c`, so the archive member the static link pulls into the exec is release-pipeline output instead of baseline output -- the first time the shipped optimizer reaches the staticlib MIR shapes on any leg, which is what lets a future optimizer regression over them RED here instead of passing green. WHY THE ARM CAN ATTRIBUTE ITS DIFFERENCE TO THE LIBRARY: `main.c` is deliberately thin -- one extern declaration and one call, no locals, no arithmetic, no inlinable callee -- so it offers the pipeline nothing of its own, while `dss_lib_answer` in dsslib.c carries an inlinable helper, a loop-invariant addend and locals for Mem2Reg to promote, and still returns exactly 42. `mustDifferFromBaseline: true` is therefore aimed AT THE PREREQUISITE BUILD: if the runner stops threading the arm's configuration into it, or if someone simplifies `dss_lib_answer` back to `return 42;`, the expectation is that the optimized exec has nothing left to differ by and the arm REDS instead of quietly asserting x == x. That expectation is INFERRED, not measured here -- but it rests on a DSS measurement of exactly this shape, recorded under D-TEST-CORPUS-77-OPTIMIZED-ARMS-WITNESS-NOTHING: a consumer whose only call was external produced a BYTE-IDENTICAL pe64 image under `debug` and `release`, and only giving the consumer an inlinable helper, an accumulator and a loop made the two configs diverge. WHAT THE PER-DEPENDENCY OPT-IN ADDS OVER THE ARM-LEVEL ONE, now that every `dependsOn` entry above also carries `mustDifferFromBaseline: true`: the ARM-LEVEL key compares the EXECUTABLE's bytes, and an exec can differ between the two configs for reasons entirely its own -- main.c's translation unit, image layout, anything the pipeline touches on the consumer side -- so a green arm-level assertion is still consistent with `dsslib.c` having been built at BASELINE the whole time. Only the PER-DEPENDENCY key compares THE PREREQUISITE'S OWN IMAGE, arm vs baseline, so it is the only form here that actually asserts the ARCHIVE was compiled through the arm's pipeline; the arm-level key cannot tell that case apart from a consumer-only difference. The key is opt-in (absent means report-only) and is honoured at every nesting depth. NO corpus dependency declared it before this manifest and fat_archive_merge's, so it shipped exercised only by the two runners' planted fixtures -- these are the first corpus dependencies to arm it. SAFE TO ARM, MEASURED (shipped CLI, Windows host, cross-compiling `dsslib.c` to each `-staticlib` and comparing debug vs release BYTE-wise, not by size): pe64-x86_64 866 -> 664, elf64-x86_64 1672 -> 1464, elf64-aarch64 1512 -> 1376, macho64-arm64 770 -> 650 -- all four DIFFER, so no armed entry is a guaranteed red. That is an image measurement, NOT a leg result. Do not re-quote those byte counts as a pin: a COFF archive embeds the source stem, so the pe64 figure moves if the file is renamed; what is asserted is the DIFFERENCE, never the size. D-LINK-NONEXTERNAL-DEFINED-SYMBOL-READ-AS-BLOCK-LABEL-NOT-ATOM -- WHY `dss_lib_step` IS NOT `static`: with the keyword, MEASURED on the same host, the exec link reds on pe64-x86_64 and macho64-arm64 with `error[K_SymbolUndefined] ... relocation in CU #N targets symbol #M which is not defined or imported in that CompilationUnit` while both elf64 legs link fine, because a relocation to a FILE-LOCAL symbol inside an archive member is not resolvable by the COFF and Mach-O readers today; it links under `release` only because inlining removes the call, which is a config-dependent escape rather than a fix. Dropping the keyword costs the arm nothing -- the helper is still inlined, the image still differs, and the pe64 exec still runs 42 at BOTH configs (MEASURED) -- and the keyword is restored when that row closes. Leg-by-leg results are NOT recorded here -- whoever runs the legs writes them.
